title: Consumer Care Note — Restart Lead for Payment Arrangements After a Long Hardship Hold
content:
The restart lead of a plan under Payment Arrangements that resumes after a hold is set by the hardship hold that suspended it.

## Rule

The hold is the one on the plan's account whose decision date is the plan's suspended date, as recorded under Hardship and Protective Holds: its start date, its ended date, its tier's documentation requirement and the financial assistance decisions the client recorded on the hold's event history. The hold's length is counted in days from its start date to its ended date.

- A hold that lasted at least 60 days, counted from its start date to its ended date, and on which the client recorded an approved-full or approved-partial financial assistance decision takes a restart lead of 22 days.
- A hold that lasted at least 60 days, needed documentation and carries no such approved decision takes 17 days.
- Any other hold takes the type's resume minimum before the next installment.

The decision that counts is the most recent financial assistance decision recorded on the hold.

## Decision grid

| Hold length (start date to ended date) | Most recent assistance decision approved full or partial | Tier needs documentation | Restart lead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 days or more | Yes | Either | 22 days |
| 60 days or more | No | Yes | 17 days |
| 60 days or more | No | No | The type's resume minimum |
| 59 days or fewer | Either | Either | The type's resume minimum |

## Hypothetical holds

- Started 1 March, ended 30 April: 60 days, which is at least 60. With an approved-partial decision recorded by the client: 22 days.
- The same hold under a tier that needs documentation, with no approved-full or approved-partial decision recorded by the client: 17 days.
- Started 1 March, ended 29 April: 59 days, under 60 — the type's resume minimum, whatever the decision.
